newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end 1.04 pct lower on VP rumour.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end 1.04 pct lower on VP rumour.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended 1.04 percent lower on Tuesday, slightly recovering after unfounded rumours over Vice President Try Sutrisno's health prompted further selling in late trade, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 7.14 points to 680.33 points after touching a low of 677.14 points.
Losers led gainers by 76 to 40, with 59 counters unchanged.
"Profit-taking had been underway since the morning but a rumour that Vice President Sutrisno had died prompted further selling," one local broker said.
Another local broker said he believed the rumour would not have much affect on Wednesday, with active trading expected in companies of the diversified Lippo Group.
Sutrisno was due to attend a fast-breaking meal with senior government officials later on Tuesday, an official from the vice-president's office said.
"He's fine. He has no official programme today but later in the evening will attend a fast breaking meal with senior government officials," the official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
Lippo group's retailer Multipolar and Matahari were actively targetted for buying by local and foreign investors, brokers said.
They said this was due to their fundamentals after Multipolar won shareholders' approval to proceed with its plan to take a 50.1 percent controlling interest in Matahari.
"I heard Matahari will upgrade their 1997 net profit target following its alliance with the Lippo Group," a broker with a foreign firm said.
Lippo Securities, Lippo Life and Lippo Karawaci were also active traded on expectations of better 1996 results, brokers said.
Profit-taking in heavyweights telecommunications firm Telkom and cigarette makers Gudang Garam and Sampoerna helped push down the index, brokers said.
The three stocks have a combined weighting of 34.33 percent on the index.
Telkom fell 75 rupiah to 4,125 rupiah on a volume of 2.8 million shares, while Gudang Garam fell 475 rupiah to 10,725 rupiah on 1.3 million shares.

Brokers also said Gudang Garam was down due to expectations of slow growth in 1997. One analyst said he was cautious over whether the firm could maintain a strong 1996 performance in 1997 after raising prices in the past year.
